content.text: Synthetic documents allow researchers to vary typography, page geometry and visual complexity while retaining exact annotations. This example combines paragraphs, a captioned figure and tables with merged headers. The chart contains illustrative values rather than measurements from an experiment.

A useful benchmark must distinguish a change in page layout from a change in content. The same source can be rendered as a technical report, an illustrated paper or a landscape reference sheet. Ground truth should follow the visible fragments on each page rather than describing invisible or discarded source elements.

content.text: Tables are rendered as vector grids with ordinary searchable text. Every logical cell has a stable source identifier and every visible fragment has its own page coordinates. Captions remain attached to their figures, while full-width elements can interrupt a multi-column text flow.

rows.text: Borders follow row and column spans.
A single cell bbox covers the merged region.
Row groups continue on the next page or column without splitting merged cells.
Repeated headers retain source-cell IDs but receive distinct visible IDs.
Actual image dimensions determine the rendered aspect ratio.
The image bbox excludes its caption.
Text wraps inside a measured allocation and remains with the figure.
Caption blocks and their text lines reference the owner.
The scan image can rotate and shear.
The same transform is applied to cells, text lines and captions.
